source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: Jerami Grant
injuries.short_comment: Grant (calf) is out for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves.
injuries.long_comment: Grant went down early in Thursday's win over the Warriors, and he's now dealing with a strained left calf that could cost him multiple contests. With Cameron Boozer (ankle) also sidelined, Taylor Hendricks and Olivier-Maxence Prosper are both worthy of streaming consideration in fantasy leagues.

injuries.name: Ty Jerome
injuries.short_comment: Jerome (hip) is probable for Saturday's game in Minnesota.
injuries.long_comment: Jerome is set to return from a three-game layoff Saturday, which will likely shift Cam Spencer back to the second unit. Jerome has gotten off to a hot start this season, averaging 25.4 points, 5.3 assists and 2.5 triples per contest on 48.5 percent shooting from the field and 90.2 percent at the line.

injuries.name: Scotty Pippen Jr.
injuries.short_comment: Pippen (back) is progressing in his recovery but is still considered week-to-week.
injuries.long_comment: Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue seeing increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

injuries.name: Javon Small
injuries.short_comment: Small won't play Saturday against the Timberwolves due to personal reasons.
injuries.long_comment: It's unclear exactly what Small is dealing with, but for now, he can be considered questionable for Monday's meeting in Charlotte. With Small out, Cam Spencer and Jahmai Mashack will fill the minutes behind Ty Jerome.

injuries.name: Cameron Boozer
injuries.short_comment: Boozer is out for Saturday's game against Minnesota due to a right ankle sprain.
injuries.long_comment: The rookie sensation is sitting out for the first time this year and can be deemed day-to-day for the time being. His absence puts a ton of pressure on Ty Jerome (hip), who's set to return from a three-game layoff, and opens up a spot in the starting lineup likely for Isaiah Stewart.

injuries.name: Richie Saunders
injuries.short_comment: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long_comment: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

injuries.name: GG Jackson
injuries.short_comment: Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months.
injuries.long_comment: Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

injuries.name: Donte DiVincenzo
injuries.short_comment: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
injuries.long_comment: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

injuries.name: Jaylen Clark
injuries.short_comment: Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks.
injuries.long_comment: Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

injuries.name: Anthony Edwards
injuries.short_comment: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
injuries.long_comment: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.
